descriptors.definition: Non-assurance services provided by practicing chartered accountants are standardized under specific related services frameworks. These include agreed-upon procedures and financial compilation engagements where no truth and fairness opinion is expressed.
inclusion: Tax return preparation without assurance
Consulting and advisory engagements
Agreed-upon procedures engagements
exclusion: Engagements involving the expression of an audit opinion
Engagements providing direct assurance to users
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from assurance engagements by the absence of an evaluation conclusion designed to enhance user confidence.

descriptors.concept_name: SRS 4400 Engagements to Perform Agreed-Upon Procedures Regarding Financial Information
descriptors.definition: An auditor carries out audit-nature procedures agreed upon with the entity and appropriate third parties to issue a factual findings report. No assurance is expressed, leaving users to draw their own conclusions.
inclusion: Procedures concerning individual financial data items
Comparison of supplier statements to trial balances
exclusion: Engagements providing an audit opinion
Reviews of financial statements expressing limited assurance
nearby_distinctions: Differs from audits and reviews because it entirely omits the expression of an assurance conclusion.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner performs agreed-upon audit-nature procedures with the entity and specified third parties to report factual findings. The engagement produces a restricted report devoid of any assurance conclusions.
inclusion: Carrying out specific verification steps on accounts
Reporting actual numerical variations without assurance
exclusion: Expressing an audit opinion
Providing general public assurance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard audits by restricting report distribution and omitting professional assurance.

descriptors.definition: An audit yields an opinion providing user assurance, whereas an agreed-upon procedures engagement reports only factual findings without any assurance. Users independently assess the reported findings to draw their own conclusions.
inclusion: Comparison of supplier names and balances
Obtaining and comparing third-party confirmations
exclusion: Issuing an opinion on financial statements taken as a whole
Providing moderate or high assurance
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with statutory audits which inherently require an expression of an opinion on truth and fairness.

descriptors.concept_name: General Principles of an Agreed-upon Procedures Engagement
descriptors.definition: The auditor must comply with ICAI ethical principles like integrity and objectivity while planning and executing agreed-upon procedures. Independence is not mandatory unless specifically required by engagement terms.
inclusion: Documenting key terms via an engagement letter
Stating lack of independence in the report if applicable
exclusion: Mandatory independence across all engagement instances
Performing procedures constituting an audit or review
nearby_distinctions: Unlike assurance engagements, independence is optional unless specified by the objective or terms of the engagement.

descriptors.definition: The factual findings report must detail the purpose and agreed procedures sufficiently while explicitly stating that no audit or review was performed. It requires specific elements including a restricted distribution statement and concrete exceptions found.
inclusion: Listing specific procedures performed
Describing errors and exceptions discovered
exclusion: Expressing an opinion or conclusion on the financial statements
Unrestricted public distribution of findings
nearby_distinctions: Differs from audit reports by omitting an opinion paragraph and explicitly denying the expression of assurance.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must maintain documentation that provides evidence supporting the reported factual findings and demonstrates that the engagement adhered to relevant standards and terms. This documentation forms the evidentiary basis for the issued report.
inclusion: Working papers supporting specific factual findings
Records showing compliance with professional standards
exclusion: Evidence required for statutory audit opinions
Documentation for unperformed procedures
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on supporting factual outcomes of agreed procedures rather than forming an overall audit opinion.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners assist management in preparing and presenting historical financial information using accounting expertise without gathering evidence for assurance. The standard applies equally to compilation engagements for other financial or non-financial information.
inclusion: Assisting management with mandatory periodic reporting
Preparing financial information for internal management use
exclusion: Engagements requiring audit opinions or review conclusions
Verifying accuracy or completeness of provided source data
nearby_distinctions: Unlike review or audit engagements, compilers do not verify information accuracy or gather evidence for conclusions.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner applies accounting and financial reporting expertise to help management prepare and present financial information under an applicable framework. The engagement concludes with a compilation report matching standard requirements without assurance.
inclusion: Applying technical accounting knowledge to draft statements
Issuing a compilation report
exclusion: Providing assurance on financial statements
Independent verification of underlying source data
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes technical preparation assistance rather than independent investigative auditing.

descriptors.definition: Compilation scope involves assisting management in preparing financial information based on management-provided data under a chosen reporting framework. Management retains full responsibility for the financial information, accounting policies, and estimates.
inclusion: Assisting with entity-specific accounting bases
Working with management-prepared draft statements
exclusion: Practitioner assumption of management financial preparation responsibilities
Independent testing of internal controls for assurance
nearby_distinctions: Management retains ultimate responsibility for judgments and estimates, while the practitioner merely applies technical compilation expertise.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners must adhere to relevant ethical requirements and identify and address threats to compliance. Because compilation is a non-assurance service, standard independence rules do not apply unless mandated by specific laws.
inclusion: Identifying ethical threats during compilation
Complying with statutory independence rules if prescribed
exclusion: Universal enforcement of strict independence for all compilations
Assurance-level ethical constraints
nearby_distinctions: Independence rules are non-mandatory for compilations unless specific local regulations dictate otherwise.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners must formally agree on engagement terms with management in writing before performing a compilation. Management remains explicitly responsible for the financial framework, internal controls, and data completeness.
inclusion: Documenting terms in an engagement letter prior to work
Evaluating recurring engagement continuance criteria
exclusion: Accepting engagements without agreed terms
Practitioner assumption of internal control maintenance
nearby_distinctions: Requires explicit written agreement regarding data completeness responsibilities before engagement execution begins.
